But the narrative contains several claims that are wrong or unsupported, and it is internally inconsistent about the documentation evidence. An investigator would need to recheck some of it.","problems":["Says the 99215 share is \"several times the all-provider share within each of those tiers\" (0-2 conditions). The card shows 0.111 vs 0.018, 0.225 vs 0.03 and 0.294 vs 0.049, so this holds for those tiers, but it does not hold for 5+ (0.0 vs 0.211), and the headline's \"every complexity tier\" overreaches.","Says \"the rule check found the result not lopsided\", but no tool output supports this. It is also at odds with the 25% vs 0% comparison stated earlier.","Describes the sampled 99215s as \"mostly single-complaint or follow-up visits\". The card has no visit-type data, so this is unsupported. Also, C0014463 is coded J06.9, a minor upper respiratory diagnosis, which the card does not frame as a complaint or follow-up.","The headline's claim of too few charts is undercut by the 'leaning' of pattern_consistent_with_upcoding, and the summary is inconsistent about how strong the evidence is.","Describes C0014495 as low back pain and C0014597 as rash. The card shows C0014495 coded M54.50 (back pain), which fits, but C0014597 is coded R21, which means rash, so that is acceptable. The \"templated or inflated notes\" speculation is not grounded in the card.","The cited examples are thin. C0014628 is the only documented one cited and is documented at moderate, and the example list is just the first low-complexity claims. It does not cite any of the documented supported 99215s or the below-billed 99214s.","\"Sampling plan in the recovery packet\" refers to an artifact not shown. Rationale is long and repetitive."]}
